metadata.summary: Adrian Newey suspects Christian Horner did not "fully understand" his "pain and frustration" during Red Bull's fallow years with Renault engines after criticism of him in the former team principal's new book.
metadata.content: Adrian Newey responds to Christian Horner's criticism of him in new book over Red Bull's struggles with Renault in 2014 | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Adrian Newey responds to Christian Horner's criticism of him in new book over Red Bull's struggles with Renault in 2014 In his autobiography, ex-Red Bull boss Christian Horner claims Adrian Newey" wanted to abandon ship" at "first sign of adversity" at team in 2014; watch every United States GP session live on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 10pm on Saturday and the race at 8pm on Sunday Friday 23 October 2026 23:38, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Adrian Newey addressed Christian Horner's criticism made in his latest memoirs. Adrian Newey suspects Christian Horner did not "fully understand" his "pain and frustration" during Red Bull's fallow years with Renault engines after criticism of him in the former team principal's new book. Horner as team principal and Newey as technical chief worked together with huge success across 19 years at Red Bull, enjoying two periods of sustained title-winning form with first Sebastian Vettel in 2010-2013 and then Max Verstappen in 2021-2024. But between those periods Red Bull took a back seat to Mercedes' dominance of the sport following the arrival of turbo-hybrid engines in 2014. messages.text: 'A clear red' - Should Ipswich's Diop have been sent off?

metadata.summary: Issa Diop escaped what Oliver Glasner called "a clear red card" during Ipswich's 1-1 draw with Nottingham Forest - but the incident split opinion, so was it the right call or not?
metadata.content: Ipswich's Issa Diop escaped a red card for a foul on Nottingham Forest's James McAtee - but was it the right call? | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Ipswich's Issa Diop escaped a red card for a foul on Nottingham Forest's James McAtee - but was it the right call? Ipswich's Issa Diop was shown a yellow card for a last-man foul on James McAtee when it was deemed he didn't deny an obvious goal-scoring opportunity by referee Thomas Bramall after a VAR intervention; Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner said it was a 'clear red card' after the 1-1 draw Friday 23 October 2026 23:57, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Should Issa Diop have seen red for his challenge on James McAtee that he only got a yellow card for? Issa Diop escaped what Oliver Glasner called "a clear red card" during Ipswich's 1-1 draw with Nottingham Forest - but the incident split opinion, so was it the right call or not? With less than five minutes of the second half played when Diop slid in on Forest's James McAtee, a sending off could have transformed the outcome of the game. Glasner was adamant Diop had denied a clear goal-scoring opportunity. But Diop himself told Sky Sports he was "quite confident" he would stay on the field as the officials and VAR came to their decision. There was also split opinion among the Sky Sports pundits, too. messages.text: Leclerc edges Antonelli to complete US GP practice double

metadata.summary: Ferrari's Charles Leclerc edged out Kimi Antonelli to complete a Friday practice double at the United States Grand Prix.
metadata.content: United States GP: Charles Leclerc edges Kimi Antonelli in Practice Two to complete Friday double for Ferrari | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content United States GP: Charles Leclerc edges Kimi Antonelli in Practice Two to complete Friday double for Ferrari Charles Leclerc tops both Friday practice sessions in Austin; Ferrari driver edged out Kimi Antonelli in second practice; watch every United States GP session live on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 10pm on Saturday and the race at 8pm on Sunday Saturday 24 October 2026 01:11, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Friday's practice sessions at the United States Grand Prix. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc edged out Kimi Antonelli to complete a Friday practice double at the United States Grand Prix. After narrowly topping Red Bull's Max Verstappen in the opening session, Leclerc improved by almost eight tenths of a second later in the day to finish 0.042s clear of Mercedes' Antonelli, who could become Formula 1's youngest ever world champion on Sunday. Verstappen appears to be in contention to extend his streak of two successive victories after finishing the second session in third, within a couple of tenths of Leclerc's leading time of 1:35.291s. metadata.summary: Christian Wade equalled Chris Ashton's top-flight try-scoring record as he inspired Newcastle to their first Gallagher Prem win of the season over Sale.
metadata.content: Christian Wade equals try-scoring record as Newcastle beat Sale in Gallagher Prem | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Christian Wade equals try-scoring record as Newcastle beat Sale in Gallagher Prem Christian Wade scores 101st top-flight try to equal Chris Ashton's record as Newcastle Red Bulls secure their first Gallagher Prem win of the season with a 17-3 triumph over Sale Sharks; Gloucester stay top of the table with a 23-5 victory against Bath Friday 23 October 2026 22:37, UK Image: Newcastle Red Bulls' Christian Wade celebrates equalling Chris Ashton's top-flight try-scoring record Christian Wade equalled Chris Ashton's top-flight try-scoring record as he inspired Newcastle to their first Gallagher Prem win of the season over Sale. Wade matched Ashton's 101 tries when he sprinted over in the 49th minute as Red Bulls recovered from a 3-0 interval deficit to blow Sale away 17-3 at Kingston Park. Newcastle captain George McGuigan grabbed the other home try, with Josh Hodge adding seven points from his boot. Svitolina announced the end of one of tennis' most high-profile relationships in an emotional post on Instagram earlier this week, where she attributed the split in part to the mental toll of Russia's ongoing war in her native Ukraine. That promoted a wave of hostility online towards the world No 6, which increased when she then confirmed that the end of the marriage had led Monfils to retire earlier than planned. messages.text: Leclerc tops first USA practice as upgraded Ferrari shows early promise

metadata.summary: Charles Leclerc showed early promise in an upgraded Ferrari car to pip Red Bull's in-form Max Verstappen to the fastest time of first practice at the United States Grand Prix.
metadata.content: United States GP: Charles Leclerc fastest in upgraded Ferrari in first practice in Austin as Mercedes rivals introduce updates | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content United States GP: Charles Leclerc fastest in upgraded Ferrari in first practice in Austin as Mercedes rivals introduce updates Ferrari, Red Bull, McLaren and Mercedes separated by narrow margins around COTA in Practice One; Antonelli in sixth on weekend he could clinch world title; watch second practice later on Friday at 10pm live on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at the same time on Saturday Friday 23 October 2026 21:49, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ted Kravitz talks through Ferrari's fourth and final upgrades for the United States Grand Prix. Charles Leclerc showed early promise in an upgraded Ferrari car to pip Red Bull's in-form Max Verstappen to the fastest time of first practice at the United States Grand Prix. Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull all introduced fresh revisions to their cars for the opening hour of running at the Circuit of the Americas, which is staging the first leg of the sport's second of three end-of-season triple headers. Ferrari's package features changes to their car's floor, sidepod and diffuser and showed speed on both the medium and soft tyres around the undulating COTA lap, with Leclerc ultimately setting the session's pace on the latter with a best lap of 1:36.052.
